name: ACRCloud
type: Identifier (commercial audio fingerprinting API, also offers cover-song and broadcast-monitoring add-ons)
maintainer: ACRCloud Corp (commercial vendor, HQ China/Germany, data centers in multiple global regions)
method: Server-side audio fingerprinting (acoustic fingerprint matched against a reference database); also offers a separate 'Cover Song Identification' product using different matching logic, and file/URL scanning tools (including direct YouTube/TikTok/Instagram URL ingestion) that download and fingerprint media server-side
required_input: Raw audio/video bytes (file upload, base64, or streamed buffer) or a source URL (YouTube/TikTok/Instagram/Facebook/Twitter) that ACRCloud's own scanning tools fetch server-side; NOT raw page HTML or title text
minimum_clip_length: ~10 seconds per single-request SDK recognition attempt (docs: 'SDKs will use 10 seconds of an audio clip for the recognition of a single request'); shorter samples reduce match probability
classification_or_hitrate: Not independently benchmarked with a published percentage; vendor claims 'one of the world's largest' reference databases (150M+ tracks) with daily updates. [uncertain] No third-party accuracy percentage found.
pitch_speed_cover_robustness: Standard music-recognition fingerprinting is not advertised as robust to cover versions or heavy pitch/speed edits -- ACRCloud sells 'Cover Song Identification' as a distinct, separately-purchased product specifically because standard fingerprint matching fails on covers/live versions. Nightcore/sped-up/pitch-shifted reuploads are not addressed in public docs. [uncertain]
catalog_language_bias: Vendor claims 'Global Coverage' sourced from 'Major PROs & Labels' with daily updates, plus direct matching against Spotify/Apple Music/Deezer/YouTube catalogs. No public breakdown by K-pop/J-pop/C-pop/anime/VTuber/indie coverage was found; ACRCloud is HQ'd partly in China and markets itself for APAC broadcast monitoring, suggesting comparatively stronger Asian-market coverage than some Western-only competitors, but this is inferential. [uncertain]
evaluation_dataset: No public evaluation dataset or benchmark methodology disclosed; all coverage/accuracy claims are vendor-stated marketing figures, not third-party benchmarked against AudioSet/GTZAN/MUSAN/MagnaTagATune/MAEB. [uncertain]
confidence_calibration: Identification responses include a numeric 'score' field (0-100) per match candidate that can be used as a threshold, but ACRCloud does not publish calibration guidance (e.g., precision/recall at given score cutoffs); developers must empirically tune the threshold themselves. [uncertain]
api_availability: Commercial, keyed API requiring an access_key/access_secret pair per project ('bucket'). 14-day free trial with full API access and no credit card required; after trial, pricing is tiered/custom and not published publicly (requires contacting sales or logging into the console). No perpetual free tier confirmed. [uncertain] on exact post-trial pricing.
audio_access_requirement: Requires raw audio bytes (a real audio/video sample), not just metadata. In a Chrome extension context this means capturing tab audio (e.g., chrome.tabCapture, which needs a user gesture) or downloading the source video, which will fail on DRM-protected or age-restricted/gated YouTube content that cannot be captured or fetched normally.
client_vs_server: Because of the HMAC secret, the practical architecture sends the audio sample (or its derived fingerprint) from the user's machine to a developer-controlled backend, which then calls ACRCloud -- so raw audio leaves the client machine to at least one intermediary server, with privacy/Chrome-Web-Store-disclosure implications for a karaoke extension.
bundle_weight_cold_start: No SDK/model needs to ship inside the extension bundle itself (recognition happens server-side), so client bundle weight is minimal; latency is dominated by network round-trip to upload a ~10s audio clip plus ACRCloud server processing time, not by a large downloaded model. [uncertain] on precise round-trip milliseconds.
breakage_risk: Official, actively maintained commercial API with SLA-backed uptime (not a scraped/unofficial surface), so breakage risk from ACRCloud's own infrastructure is low; the higher risk is business risk (pricing changes, trial expiry, account suspension) rather than technical breakage.
realtime_capability: Response for a single ~10s clip is typically sub-few-seconds server-side, but overall in-browser perceived latency also includes capturing the audio sample and (if used) the backend-proxy hop, so it is 'near real-time' (seconds, not milliseconds) rather than truly instant. [uncertain] exact published latency figure.
identification_fields: Returns title, artist(s), album, release date, label, and a numeric match score; also provides external IDs/links to Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, YouTube, and standard industry identifiers ISRC and UPC/ISWC when available via the linked Music Metadata product.
isrc_availability: Yes -- ACRCloud explicitly advertises ISRC (and ISWC/UPC) as part of its identification/metadata response, making it usable as a join key for downstream lookups.
karaoke_specific_outputs: No BPM, musical key, vocal/instrumental stem separation, or word-level lyric timing in the core Music Recognition product; ACRCloud sells separate/adjacent products (e.g., Broadcast Monitoring, Cover Song ID) but no confirmed karaoke-grade timing output. [uncertain]
tos_restrictions: As a paid commercial service, ACRCloud's ToS govern permitted use of returned metadata (e.g., restrictions on reselling raw recognition results, and per-plan usage caps); ACRCloud itself scrapes/downloads YouTube and social URLs server-side on the customer's behalf via its File Scanning tool, which shifts YouTube-ToS exposure onto ACRCloud's own infrastructure rather than the extension developer for that specific workflow. Full legal terms require reviewing ACRCloud's current Terms of Service document directly. [uncertain] on exact current clause wording.
risk_tolerance_note: Because ACRCloud is an official, contractually-licensed commercial vendor (not a scraped/reverse-engineered surface like ytInitialData or SongRec), it carries materially lower legal/ToS risk than the unofficial options in this comparison set -- the trade-off is cost and secret-key handling complexity rather than legal exposure.
cascade_position: Best suited as an enrichment or fallback step (not a cheap always-on gate) given its per-request cost and signing overhead; would typically run only after a cheaper music-vs-non-music classifier has already gated out non-music content.
failure_mode: Fails relatively silently (no-match / empty result with a low score) rather than confidently hallucinating a wrong title/artist, because it is fingerprint-based matching against a real reference database rather than generative guessing -- reduces risk of a visibly wrong karaoke overlay, though false-positive risk still exists for very similar tracks/remixes.
cost_model_at_scale: Post-trial pricing is not publicly published (custom/tiered, contact-sales model); competitors in this space typically price in the few-dollars-per-1,000-requests range, so at realistic per-session repeated-use load (multiple identification calls per user per day) costs could scale into meaningful recurring spend for a free consumer extension. [uncertain] exact rate.
geo_region_availability: Operates multiple regional data centers/endpoints (e.g., identify-eu-west-1, identify-us-west-2, identify-ap-southeast-1) so requests can be routed to the nearest region; no evidence of hard geo-blocking of the API itself, though catalog completeness may vary by region/label licensing. [uncertain] on any region-specific catalog gaps.
